newsitem.title: FINLAND: OUTOKUMPU SAYS ALL TARA CLAIMS DISMISSED.
newsitem.headline: OUTOKUMPU SAYS ALL TARA CLAIMS DISMISSED.

text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy said on Thursday all claims against it -- ranging from 139-327 million Irish pounds -- in a dispute over Europe's largest zinc mine, Tara in Ireland, had been dismissed.

"The judgment dismissed all allegations of wrongdoing and rejected all claims for damages," Outokumpu said in a statement referring to an Irish High Court decision on litigation started in 1986 against it, its Irish unit Tara Mines Ltd and others.
Outokumpu said Bula Ltd, an Irish company in receivership, filed the claims against Tara, Outokumpu, the Irish energy minister and various private persons in 1986.
Tara Mines owns and operates the Tara zinc mine next door to an ore body owned by Bula Ltd.

The allegations included trespass and ore theft, civil conspiracy and breach of Tara's state mining lease to prevent Bula from developing its part of the ore body and force Bula to sell its ore body to Tara at below market value, Outokumpu said.
Tara's annual production is about 165,000 tonnes of zinc and 45,000 tonnes of lead concentrate, Outokumpu added.
